rationale: Fidelity, diversity and memorization measured in lognorm_pca50 (a domain-appropriate space: Inception features would be mis-specified for these data); utility via a downstream classifier. Primary metric 'target_class_recall_gain' is the quantity the objective asks to improve.

decision: Adopt generative augmentation, with an explicit caveat for Megakaryocytes
rationale: The objective asks for synthetic rare-class cells, and the imbalance ratio is 76.3. Dendritic cells (37 cells, about 26 in train after the 0.2/0.1 split) are enough for a conditional decoder that shares structure with the other 2,600 cells. Megakaryocytes (15 cells, about 10 in train, about 3 in test) are at the memorisation limit. The plan keeps them as a target but caps their synthetic count, checks memorisation, and requires the augmented classifier to beat class_weighted_classifier. If it does not, the conclusion is that class weighting alone is enough for that class.

alternatives_rejected.option: No generative model; use class_weighted_classifier only
alternatives_rejected.reason: The objective explicitly asks for synthetic cells, and DC (37) can support a conditional generator. Class-weighting is kept as the baseline to beat, not as a replacement.

decision: Set beta and weight_decay explicitly for nb_vae, and n_layers explicitly for vae
rationale: Light weight decay limits overfitting to the about 10 Megakaryocyte training cells, which the conditional decoder could otherwise memorise. Pinning beta and n_layers makes the two models identical in architecture, so their comparison isolates the likelihood. 400 epochs at about 15 steps per epoch (n_train about 1,850 / 128) is about 6,000 updates. For a 2,000-gene, 128-unit network this should fit within 480 s, so the epoch count was not reduced.

alternatives_rejected.reason: With n_over_p = 0.081 (n ≈ 1,850 vs 2,000 HVGs) and very few rare-class cells, extra capacity mainly increases the risk of memorisation.
ZINB is preferred for only 2.3% of genes, the median zero-inflation pi is 0.016, and excess zeros vs NB are -0.029. The data do not support the extra parameter.

decision: Add AUPRC as a supporting utility metric; keep target_class_recall_gain as primary
rationale: With a 0.2 test fraction, the test set holds only about 3 Megakaryocytes and about 7 Dendritic cells. Recall on 3 cells moves in steps of 33 percentage points, so the primary metric is very noisy. Per-class AUPRC does not depend on a threshold and uses the classifier's ranking of all test cells. It is a steadier check on whether the gain is real. Read the memorisation metric carefully for the target classes: with about 10 real Megakaryocytes in training, synthetic cells sitting at nearest-neighbour distance to real training cells would mean the model is copying them.

alternatives_rejected.reason: The objective is about rare-class performance. Macro-F1 averages in 6 well-populated classes, which dilutes the signal, and it is still threshold-dependent.

alternatives_rejected.option: Raise test_fraction to 0.3 to get more rare test cells
alternatives_rejected.reason: It would add only about 1 Megakaryocyte to the test set while taking away about 1.5 of the 10 training cells. That trade hurts the generator more than it helps the estimate.

chosen: PCA(50) of log-normalised expression of 2000 highly variable genes
rationale: Fitted on real training data only.

The run is adequate for the objective. On the primary metric, nb_vae lifts target-class recall from 0.690 to 1.000 (gain +0.310, 95% CI [0.00, 0.69], P(gain>0)=0.94). Against the class-weighted baseline the gain is +0.238 (CI [0.00, 0.60], P=0.88). Macro-F1 also rises slightly, +0.024, but that CI [-0.037, 0.136] includes zero. Overall fidelity is close to the real-holdout reference: Fréchet 12.4 vs 11.0, MMD 0.0088 vs 0.0048, marginal KS 0.047 vs 0.027, coverage 0.967 vs 0.998, precision 0.973 vs 0.999. Count marginals also match well: zero fraction 0.9255 vs 0.9257 and gene-mean correlation 0.998. No memorisation was flagged (DCR ratio 1.04, no exact copies, 1.6% too-close). The main weakness is Megakaryocytes: per-class coverage and recall are both 0.2 and density is 0.28, so the synthetic cells probably cover only part of that class. That estimate rests on just 5 holdout cells, though. The primary metric can't go higher. Augmented target-class recall is already 1.000, so no revision could raise target_class_recall_gain above +0.310, and a revision is only kept if the primary metric improves. Retraining would spend compute with no possible payoff on that metric. The intervals are also very wide because the target classes have only a handful of test cells: real-only recalls of 0.714 and 0.667 point to roughly 7 and 3 cells. Any further change would be measured on noise. nb_vae clearly beats the Gaussian VAE on fidelity (Fréchet 12.4 vs 24.6, MMD 0.0088 vs 0.0207, marginal KS 0.047 vs 0.406, Dendritic-cell precision 0.92 vs 0.31). Both models give the same primary gain, so there is no reason to switch. Training stopped early and cleanly at epoch 133 of 158, well under the 400-epoch cap, and the gap between train loss (480) and validation loss (492) is small. Neither suggests a hyperparameter problem.

alternatives_rejected.option: retune nb_vae (e.g. lower beta to 0.5, or raise latent_dim) to improve Megakaryocyte coverage (0.2)
alternatives_rejected.reason: Target recall is already 1.000, so the primary metric can't improve and the revision would be thrown away. The Megakaryocyte coverage figure rests on 5 holdout and 10 training cells, which is too few to tell a real gap from chance. A lower beta also raises the memorisation risk for a 10-cell class.

It gives the same primary gain (+0.310) but much worse fidelity: Fréchet 24.6, marginal KS 0.41, Dendritic-cell precision 0.31 and Megakaryocyte recall 0.0. Its macro-F1 is no better than the class-weighted baseline (-0.001).
The profile prefers ZINB for only 2.3% of genes, and NB already matches the zero fraction almost exactly (0.9255 vs 0.9257). The primary metric is also already at its maximum.
This would drop the count likelihood that is working well here. A diffusion model is also more likely to memorise a 10-cell class, and it cannot beat a primary metric that is already at its maximum.

evidence.expected_effect: None; no revision is proposed. Target-class recall gain stays at +0.310, which is the most it can be, with nb_vae fidelity close to the real-holdout reference. Before relying on the size of the gain, re-check it on a larger or repeated (cross-validated) split, because the lower end of the CI sits at 0.
